title: Магнитное поле параллельных токов
prompt:
6 infinitely long straight thin wires are perpendicular to the xy-plane (the page) and pass through the following points (coordinates in centimetres):
wire 1: through (8, 7), current 7 A out of the page (+z)
wire 2: through (-5, 5), current 10 A into the page (−z)
wire 3: through (6, -9), current 14 A into the page (−z)
wire 4: through (0, 2), current 10 A out of the page (+z)
wire 5: through (2, 0), current 12 A into the page (−z)
wire 6: through (6, 0), current 13 A into the page (−z)

The wires are in vacuum, μ0 = 4π·10⁻⁷ T·m/A. Each wire produces the field of magnitude μ0·I/(2πr) circling it by the right-hand rule: for a current out of the page the field lines go counterclockwise as seen by a reader looking at the page (x-axis to the right, y-axis up, +z toward the reader). Find the magnitude of the total magnetic field at the point P = (-1, -5), in microtesla (μT), with 4 significant figures.

Think it through, then finish with a final line of the form `ANSWER: <your answer>`.

title: Давление в трубопроводе
prompt:
Water (density 1000 kg/m³, incompressible) flows steadily at a volume flow rate of 7 L/s through a pipeline of 6 sections connected one after another:
section 1: cross-section 123 cm², centreline elevation 11.2 m; loss coefficient of the connection to section 2: K = 0.2
section 2: cross-section 80 cm², centreline elevation 9.5 m; loss coefficient of the connection to section 3: K = 1.3
section 3: cross-section 17 cm², centreline elevation 11.8 m; loss coefficient of the connection to section 4: K = 0.4
section 4: cross-section 44 cm², centreline elevation 18.2 m; loss coefficient of the connection to section 5: K = 0.8
section 5: cross-section 44 cm², centreline elevation 23.0 m; loss coefficient of the connection to section 6: K = 1.2
section 6: cross-section 129 cm², centreline elevation 19.6 m

In every section the speed is uniform over the cross-section (v = Q/A). Between section i and section i + 1 the flow loses pressure Δp_loss = K·ρ·v_i²/2, where v_i is the speed in the upstream section i; otherwise the Bernoulli equation holds: p + ρv²/2 + ρgz is conserved. Use g = 9.8 m/s². The absolute pressure in section 1 is 375 kPa.

Find the absolute pressure in section 6, in kPa, with 4 significant figures.

Think it through, then finish with a final line of the form `ANSWER: <your answer>`.

title: Смещение луча в слоистой пластине
prompt:
A narrow light ray in air (refractive index exactly 1) falls on the flat top surface of a stack of 2 transparent plane-parallel layers at an angle of incidence of 52° (measured from the normal). The layers are listed from top to bottom; they are in direct contact, all interfaces are parallel, and below the last layer there is air again.

layer 1: refractive index 2.32, thickness 15 mm
layer 2: refractive index 1.45, thickness 14 mm

The ray passes through all layers (ignore reflections) and emerges into the air below. Find the lateral displacement of the ray: the perpendicular distance between the straight line of the incident ray (extended through the stack) and the emergent ray. Give it in mm with 4 significant figures.

Think it through, then finish with a final line of the form `ANSWER: <your answer>`.

title: Пакет задач TheoremQA: тепловая и статистическая физика

source.id: physics, subfields Thermodynamics, Statistical physics, Condensed matter physics; problem ids in task data

prompt:
Below are 5 independent physics problems on thermal, statistical and condensed-matter physics. Solve each of them.

Problem 1.
Light of wavelength 400 nm is incident upon lithium (phi = 2.93 eV). Calculate the photon energy in eV.
[Answer unit: eV]

Problem 2.
A surveyor uses a steel measuring tape that is exactly 50.000 m long at a temperature of 20°C. The markings on the tape are calibrated for this temperature. When it is 35°C, the surveyor uses the tape to measure a distance. The value that she reads off the tape is 35.794 m. What is the actual distance? (Unit: m)
[Answer unit: m]

Problem 3.
Find the fraction of the standard solar flux reaching the Earth (about 1000 W/m^22) available to a solar collector lying flat on the Earth’s surface at Regina, Saskatchewan (latitude 50°N) at noon on the summer solstice.
[Answer unit: dimensionless fraction]

Problem 4.
A camper pours 0.300 kg of coffee, initially in a pot at 70.0°C into a 0.120-kg aluminum cup initially at 20.0°C. What is the equilibrium temperature? Assume that coffee has the same specific heat as water and that no heat is exchanged with the surroundings. (Unit: °C)
[Answer unit: °C]

Problem 5.
Compute the mean translational kinetic energy of a single ideal gas molecule in eV.
[Answer unit: eV (take room temperature as 293 K)]

Give the final answer as a comma-separated list of 5 numbers, one per problem in order (Problem 1 first). Write each number as a plain decimal or in e-notation (e.g. 6.2e-5), without units and without thousands separators.

Think it through, then finish with a final line of the form `ANSWER: <your answer>`.

title: Теплопередача через многослойную стенку
prompt:
A flat composite wall consists of 8 layers in perfect thermal contact, listed from the inside to the outside:
layer 1: stone, thickness 280 mm, thermal conductivity 2.3 W/(m·K)
layer 2: glass wool, thickness 40 mm, thermal conductivity 0.04 W/(m·K)
layer 3: concrete, thickness 240 mm, thermal conductivity 1.4 W/(m·K)
layer 4: clay, thickness 75 mm, thermal conductivity 1.1 W/(m·K)
layer 5: gypsum board, thickness 20 mm, thermal conductivity 0.17 W/(m·K)
layer 6: wood, thickness 10 mm, thermal conductivity 0.13 W/(m·K)
layer 7: plywood, thickness 15 mm, thermal conductivity 0.12 W/(m·K)
layer 8: gypsum board, thickness 75 mm, thermal conductivity 0.17 W/(m·K)

The inside air is at 20 °C with a convective heat-transfer coefficient of 10 W/(m²·K) at the inner surface; the outside air is at -2 °C with a coefficient of 17 W/(m²·K) at the outer surface. Heat flow is steady and one-dimensional (no radiation, no edge effects).

Find (1) the heat flux through the wall in W/m² (from inside to outside) and (2) the temperature in °C at the interface between layer 4 and layer 5. Give both with 4 significant figures, in the form `q, T`.

Think it through, then finish with a final line of the form `ANSWER: <your answer>`.
